Let
\[
J(\varepsilon)=\iint_{\mathbb R^2}e^{-(X^2-Y^3)^2-\varepsilon Y^8}\,dX\,dY .
\]
With the scaling
\[
x=n^{-1/4}X,\qquad y=n^{-1/6}Y,
\]
we get
\[
I_n=n^{-5/12}J(n^{-1/3}),
\]
because
\[
n(x^2-y^3)^2=(X^2-Y^3)^2,\qquad ny^8=n^{-1/3}Y^8.
\]
Thus the required limit is
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty} n^{1/48}\bigl(J(n^{-1/3})-J(0)\bigr)
=\lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\varepsilon^{-1/16}\bigl(J(\varepsilon)-A\bigr).
\]

For fixed \(Y\), define
\[
h(Y)=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-(X^2-Y^3)^2}\,dX.
\]
Then
\[
J(\varepsilon)-A=\int_{\mathbb R}h(Y)\bigl(e^{-\varepsilon Y^8}-1\bigr)\,dY.
\]

The main contribution comes from \(Y\to+\infty\). For \(Y>0\),
\[
h(Y)=2\int_0^\infty e^{-(X^2-Y^3)^2}\,dX.
\]
Put \(u=X^2-Y^3\). Then
\[
h(Y)=\int_{-Y^3}^{\infty} e^{-u^2}(u+Y^3)^{-1/2}\,du.
\]
Hence, as \(Y\to+\infty\),
\[
h(Y)\sim Y^{-3/2}\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}e^{-u^2}\,du
=\sqrt{\pi}\,Y^{-3/2}.
\]
For \(Y<0\), \(h(Y)\) decays faster than any power, so it does not affect the first correction term.

Therefore
\[
J(\varepsilon)-A
\sim \sqrt{\pi}\int_0^\infty Y^{-3/2}\bigl(e^{-\varepsilon Y^8}-1\bigr)\,dY.
\]
Now set \(t=\varepsilon^{1/8}Y\). Then
\[
\int_0^\infty Y^{-3/2}\bigl(e^{-\varepsilon Y^8}-1\bigr)\,dY
=\varepsilon^{1/16}\int_0^\infty t^{-3/2}(e^{-t^8}-1)\,dt.
\]
So the limit equals
\[
\sqrt{\pi}\int_0^\infty t^{-3/2}(e^{-t^8}-1)\,dt.
\]
Evaluate the integral with \(u=t^8\):
\[
\int_0^\infty t^{-3/2}(e^{-t^8}-1)\,dt
=\frac18\int_0^\infty (e^{-u}-1)u^{-17/16}\,du.
\]
For \(0<\alpha<1\),
\[
\int_0^\infty (e^{-u}-1)u^{-1-\alpha}\,du=\Gamma(-\alpha).
\]
Taking \(\alpha=1/16\),
\[
\frac18\Gamma\!\left(-\frac1{16}\right)
=\frac18\left(-16\Gamma\!\left(\frac{15}{16}\right)\right)
=-2\Gamma\!\left(\frac{15}{16}\right).
\]
Thus the required limit is
\[
\boxed{-2\sqrt{\pi}\,\Gamma\!\left(\frac{15}{16}\right)}.
\]
